text: Workers from Halvorsen Mott will rebuild the Okarra Bridge, after the firm won the contract announced at yesterday’s council session in North Okarra, according to records read aloud and a spokesman for the project office. I watched as transport chief Elin Varga confirmed the award and said the company’s bid came in at 18.4 million crowns, under the other final proposal by nearly 600,000. Varga said site prep begins Monday, with river diversions and steel deliveries expected next week. Outside the chamber, foreman Jori Senn told me Halvorsen Mott had already assigned a six-person survey crew to the east bank. The bridge has been closed since February, when flood damage widened cracks in the central span.
